pr_body:
Fix: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54102

It really isn't necessary, but also the way it was done would cause bind variables to be lost, resulting in broken queries.

issue_context.title: SQLite3::MismatchException: datatype mismatch when querying with a join to a has_many relationship that has a scope
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
I'm not totally sure this is a completely minimal reproduction, but it does appear to require a query joining via a has_many relationship that has a scope that contains a join.

I haven't observed this issue with PostgreSQL, only with SQLite.

```ruby
require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails", "~> 7.2.2.1"
  gem "sqlite3", "~> 2.5.0"
end

require "active_record/railtie"
require "minitest/autorun"

ENV["DATABASE_URL"] = "sqlite3::memory:"

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.load_defaults Rails::VERSION::STRING.to_f
  config.eager_load = false
  config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
  config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"
end

Rails.application.initialize!

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :instructors, force: true do |t|
  end

  create_table :instructor_roles, force: true do |t|
    t.integer :instructor_id
    t.integer :role_id
    t.integer :student_id
  end

  create_table :roles, force: true do |t|
  end

  create_table :students, force: true do |t|
    t.integer :status
  end
end

class Instructor < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :instructor_roles, -> { active }
end

class InstructorRole < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :instructor
  belongs_to :role
  belongs_to :student

  scope :active, -> {
    joins("JOIN students ON instructor_roles.student_id = students.id")
    .where("students.status = ?", 1)
  }
end

class Role < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :instructor_roles
end

class Student < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :instructor_roles
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_association_stuff
    # No error
    ir = InstructorRole.active.first
    # Raises an error
    i = Instructor.joins(:instructor_roles).first
  end
end

```

### Expected behavior
Not throw an exception.

### Actual behavior
`ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: SQLite3::MismatchException: datatype mismatch`

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 7.2.2.1

**Ruby version**: ruby 3.3.4 (2024-07-09 revision be1089c8ec) [arm64-darwin23]

This works in rails 7.1.5.1 and first appears in 7.2.0 (I haven't checked the beta or rc builds). It is still an issue in 8.0.1, but I can't currently update to 8.x due to other dependencies.
comments:
Bisected, error started appearing with commit 8e6a5deca626c944933211d7977f4e7e76869e74 which was part of #51139

cc @byroot

Hum. It's weird, it's like the bind argument get lost:

```
Instructor Load (0.1ms)
 SELECT "instructors".*
FROM "instructors"
INNER JOIN "instructor_roles" ON "instructor_roles"."instructor_id" = "instructors"."id"
JOIN students ON instructor_roles.student_id = students.id
AND (students.status = ?)
ORDER BY "instructors"."id" ASC
LIMIT ?
 [["LIMIT", 1]]
```
Looks like the bug is similar on other adapters (the exception is different of course, but the cause is the same, a missing bind argument).

Alright, if I rewrite the scope as:

```ruby
  scope :active, -> {
    joins("JOIN students ON instructor_roles.student_id = students.id")
    .where(students: { status: 1 })
  }
```

It also fails on `7.1.x`, which means it's a pre-existing "bug" (using quotes here because I've never seen `joins(:scope_name)`, so I don't know if it's supposed to work in the first place).

It was only working prior because using `.where("sql", bind_arg)` would cause early interpolation of the bind arguments, but it appears that for late bound scopes, the bind arguments were never merged when using `.joins(:scope_name)`.

I need to dig more in whether this is valid use of `.joins` or not.

> I need to dig more in whether this is valid use of `.joins` or not.

Nevermind, I just realized the scope is called from:

```ruby
  has_many :instructor_roles, -> { active }
```

I tried with some pretty old versions, some are hard to run now, but the bug was there at least since 6.0. I'm not even sure association scopes with bind arguments ever worked. I took a quick glance at the code and I can't seem to see any attempt at carrying the bind values over.

I forgot to say, I don't know if I'll be able to fix this in a timely manner, so if you are in search of a workaround to be able to upgrade you can do:

```ruby
  scope :active, -> {
    joins("JOIN students ON instructor_roles.student_id = students.id")
    .where(sanitize_sql_array(["students.status = ?", 1]))
  }
```

Interestingly:

```ruby
  scope :active, -> {
    joins(:student).where(students: {status: 1})
  }
```

Also works. So the binds are copied in some cases, not clear why yet it isn't when using a SQL fragment to join.
Alright, backported to 8.0 and 7.2, you should be able to use the  `7-2-stable` branch until the fix is released.
Thanks so much for the very speedy resolution (and the workarounds offered)!

review_comments: As a bonus, we no longer need to checkout the connection here. This was a big smell.
